tb21_profile.skill: Aggregate a sparse benchmark results table, keep only rows with complete task coverage, compute the mean-over-tasks, argmax it, and emit one exact identifier string
tb21_profile.domain: ML evaluation / embedding-model leaderboards (MTEB, HuggingFace org/model ids), pandas-style tabular aggregation
tb21_profile.task_form: data-analysis question-answering: read semi-structured results, filter + aggregate, write a single pinned answer to /app/result.txt

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Group-index computation returns wrong results with many grouping columns: debugging the exact pandas groupby machinery the leaderboard aggregation relies on.
pivot_table failure when unstacking; the model-by-task pivot is exactly the reshape the MTEB answer needs.
Numeric experiment results wrongly coerced to None: missing values corrupting an experiment-results table, the same failure mode.
DataFrame.compare misses differences with nullable Int64; reasoning about NA semantics when comparing result tables.
value_counts with sort=False returns wrongly ordered results; ordering bugs in aggregation output are the leaderboard's failure class.
metrics show --precision ignored; same territory of rendering model-metric tables, but the fix is cosmetic plumbing.
pd.concat broken by removed assignments; concatenating per-model result frames is the first step of the TB2.1 task.
qcut picks wrong interval bounds; numeric-binning correctness in pandas, adjacent to but not needed by the ranking task.
metrics diff vs diff JSON output inconsistency; ML-experiment tooling domain, mostly CLI output-shape reasoning.
Incorrect loss computation and activation counting; debugging a wrong evaluation metric, though unrelated to table aggregation.

Inconsistent return type from groupby-resample-count; shape/typing of aggregation results, which the leaderboard code must get right.
Warm-up compilation time leaking into recorded benchmark results: making measured benchmark numbers comparable across solvers.
Swapped off-diagonal entries in McNemar's contingency table; statistical comparison of two models, subtly wrong numbers.
Outlier data check reports rows instead of columns; auditing a results table along the correct axis, like per-task vs per-model coverage.
Dataset name with a dot breaks every benchmark; benchmark-suite plumbing rather than result aggregation.
random_state not propagated into generated pipelines; AutoML ecosystem, but reproducibility plumbing not leaderboard maths.

COALESCE(AVG(price),0) so empty groups score 0 instead of NULL; treating absent measurements as zero rather than skipping them.
Filter out NaN and sentinel 'N/A' string values correctly; the incomplete-record handling the MTEB task hinges on, at micro scale.
Pick the most common value per group key; simple argmax-per-group, strongly verified but very shallow.
Compute each office's percentage of its state total; normalising values against a group total before comparison.
Name aggregate output columns and flatten MultiIndex results; only the plumbing of a pandas aggregation transfers.

Rank 14 classifiers over 34 datasets, ignore a decoy metrics file, report the winner; same read-the-right-table-and-rank discipline.
Filter model configs on an accuracy threshold then argmax on efficiency from a JSONL results log; filter-then-argmax over model results.
Fix a buggy script that reports the wrong best algorithm family from a benchmark database; requires deriving the correct aggregation.

notes: CalibForge dominates this task outright: five of its shortlist entries are coverage-filtered model-ranking problems, and data-science_20260513_204848_003 is an embedding-leaderboard coverage audit in org/model format, i.e. effectively the same problem. Terminal-Lego contributed one genuinely useful angle retrieval missed (task_08294, task_14631: SQL aggregates where missing rows must count as zero rather than be dropped) but is otherwise pandas micro-demos and does not reach the final ten. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has no ML-benchmark content at all; its best offering is the colonies/planets join-and-aggregate family plus one argmax-over-counts task, all 'absent'-graded, so none is in final_top10 and none deserves to be. TerminalWorld is thin here and several of its highest-RRF hits (tw_733941, tw_240515, tw_101457) are FREE; I kept only non-FREE entries in per_source, so its tail is padded with generic CSV chores. SWE-Smith/SWE-Rebench are judged on skill+domain as instructed: the pandas groupby/NaN family is the honest transfer, and evalml-1221 is the single SWE-side entry strong enough for the final ten.
